concepts.title: Accelerator memory and peer dataflow
concepts.meaning: Data moves from device memory into local tiles, through compute, and across peer links when needed.
concepts.brief: Trace a working tile from device memory into on-chip local storage, through a compute engine, then over a peer link when the workload requires another device. Mark the owner and capacity boundary at each stage.
pitfalls: Capacity and bandwidth belong to specific memory levels and owners.
Peer exchange may route over a shared link or host staging; measure the actual topology.

headings: Memory paths: capacity belongs to an owner
Thread execution and matrix dataflow
Interconnect topologies: count exchanges, then measure the route

concepts.title: Adapter artifact lineage
concepts.meaning: Trainable adapter state, pruning records, resume checkpoints and exported weights follow different paths from a frozen base model.
concepts.brief: Draw two clearly separate workflows. Light-PEFT estimates masks and scores, saves records with PEFT weights, physically slices compatible base and adapter tensors, then continues with a smaller shape. Tinker keeps a frozen base with LoRA A/B updates and offers distinct training-resume state, sampler weights and merged export artifacts. Label which artifacts preserve optimizer history, which can be sampled, and the base revision needed to reproduce the result.
pitfalls: A soft mask or adapter update is not the same artifact as a physically pruned model.
A sampler snapshot does not restore optimizer state; a merged model does not preserve remote training history.
Light-PEFT tensor surgery and Tinker hosted LoRA are different implementations, not one shared lifecycle.

headings: Lifecycle: estimate, prune, continue
Checkpoints and export paths

concepts.title: End-to-end AI app contract
concepts.meaning: A request passes input validation and trusted-fact checks before an uncertain model answer can affect a decision.
concepts.brief: Follow an invented account request through input validation, trusted server-side facts, a deterministic policy check and a visible result. Preserve a trace receipt and place uncertain model output behind the application contract.
pitfalls: Client-provided facts do not become trusted because they arrived in JSON.
A well-shaped model response can still violate the underlying policy.

concepts.title: Collective reduce-scatter ownership
concepts.meaning: Matching tensor chunks reduce across ranks and each rank retains the chunk at its own index.
concepts.brief: Give four ranks four-element vectors. Reduce corresponding indices, move the completed chunks through a ring or tree schedule, and leave chunk r on rank r. Then optionally run all-gather to reconstruct the full vector everywhere. Keep rank order, communicator agreement, buffer offsets and stream completion visible.
pitfalls: Reduce-scatter leaves one reduced shard per rank; it does not leave the full tensor everywhere.
Every rank must call matching collectives in matching order with compatible arguments.
In-place reduce-scatter and all-gather use rank-offset shard locations, not automatically the buffer base.

headings: Choose the operation from desired ownership

concepts.title: GPU compiler artifact ownership
concepts.meaning: Source code is compiled into packaged device images with architecture-specific ownership and target rules.
concepts.brief: Trace one CUDA source through host compilation and device compilation into virtual and architecture-specific device images inside an executable. Highlight the artifact and diagnostic owned by each stage.
pitfalls: A host executable may contain multiple device images; source text is not the packaged artifact.
PTX and native machine code expose different compilation stages.

headings: `nvcc` packages host code with architecture-specific device images

concepts.title: Distributed object reference
concepts.meaning: A future-like handle connects a remote task result to a consumer while ownership and stored bytes have separate lifetimes.
concepts.brief: Submit several remote feature tasks and keep their ObjectRef handles at the driver. Pass top-level references directly to an actor consumer so the driver need not fetch each payload; reveal local object-store copies, reference counting, owner and reconstructable task lineage as separate layers. Contrast this with serial ray.get submission and an unbounded gather.
pitfalls: An ObjectRef is a handle and dependency, not a location or a guarantee that bytes are resident on one node.
Reference metadata and retained objects still consume resources.
Task-result lineage, actor process state and durable checkpointing are different recovery contracts.

headings: Three pieces of a running job
Keep the dependency remote
Object bytes, owners, and memory

concepts.title: Docker image layers
concepts.meaning: An image assembles reusable base and application layers into a runnable container.
concepts.brief: Stack the pinned base, dependency environment, application and scorer into an image. Show the built artifact running read-only, then mount a host directory over the copied evaluation path to reveal why filesystem boundaries matter.
pitfalls: Image layers are cached build inputs; a running container adds its own writable layer.
A bind mount can replace the directory view inside the container.

headings: A bind mount obscures the copied eval

concepts.title: Evidence-bound document answer
concepts.meaning: An approved passage supports an answer through a bound, auditable evidence receipt.
concepts.brief: Retrieve candidate passages, check access policy and bind the approved excerpt to a question-support receipt. Return the passage with provenance only after the evidence contract passes.
pitfalls: Retrieval proposes candidates and never grants authorization.
A declared fixture label is not an independent verifier judgment.

headings: Let the first answer be easy to audit

concepts.title: Evaluation slice dashboard
concepts.meaning: A suite-level score and per-slice results expose a safety failure hidden by an aggregate.
concepts.brief: Grade a frozen fixture set and place the overall score above all capability and safety slices. Keep failed or missing slices visible as release blockers even when the aggregate is strong.
pitfalls: Equal-weight fixture pass rate is not a production traffic success rate.
A missing safety slice must not silently disappear from aggregation.

headings: Extend the frozen fixture set fairly
Aggregate without hiding safety slices
Write gates in product language
Make a hold decision inspectable

concepts.title: Forecast maturity and alerts
concepts.meaning: A frozen forecast is compared with mature outcomes before an operational alert fires.
concepts.brief: Freeze forecasts before targets mature, reveal only outcomes available by the evaluation cutoff, calculate held-out residuals, then apply a separate operational alert rule to the same ledger.
pitfalls: Provisional and missing outcomes remain pending rather than counting as zero or perfect.
Forecast accuracy and alert utility answer different questions.

headings: Evaluate forecasts and operational alerts separately

concepts.title: Git regression history
concepts.meaning: Commit snapshots narrow a regression to the change that introduced it.
concepts.brief: Mark a passing commit and a failing commit on one history spine, then test a midpoint. Animate the remaining interval narrowing until a single regression change remains; keep the dirty worktree as a separate state.
pitfalls: A green working tree run is weaker evidence than a passing commit with a clean status.
Bisect identifies a first failing change only when the test is deterministic and endpoints are labeled correctly.

headings: Trace a regression through Git history
Prove it with a throwaway clone

concepts.title: From token stream to GPT checkpoint
concepts.meaning: A causal decoder predicts the next token, updates weights from loss and samples from the checkpoint.
concepts.brief: Pack a contiguous token stream into context windows and shifted next-token labels. Reveal causal attention, loss and weight update, then sample from the resulting checkpoint and resume from saved optimizer state.
pitfalls: Input tokens and next-token labels are shifted by one position.
Held-out chunks must not be concatenated into fake transitions.

headings: The causal LM contract
Train, sample, then keep going
What a resume file has to remember

concepts.title: GPU benchmark timing boundary
concepts.meaning: Host submission and asynchronous device work require a declared scope and synchronization boundary.
concepts.brief: Draw host submission and asynchronous device execution on separate lanes. Mark event boundaries and synchronization, then label whether launch, compilation, allocation, transfer and steady-state work belong in the measured interval.
pitfalls: A successful host launch return does not prove device work has completed.
Different measurement scopes need distinct labels and timing methods.

headings: Host and device asynchrony: time GPU streams separately from host launches
Gate 3: Synchronized timing and benchmark state control

concepts.title: Grouped GEMM padding and scale
concepts.meaning: Uneven expert token groups pack into an aligned M axis whose padding trades useful work for scheduling efficiency.
concepts.brief: Route tokens into four expert groups with 64, 192, 32 and 128 valid rows. Pack each segment to a declared M alignment, show the concatenated launch grid, highlight useful versus padded rows, and unpack outputs back to original token order. Compare one persistent grouped launch with separate per-expert launches while measuring total time and useful-token throughput.
pitfalls: M counts token-expert assignments, not unique source tokens.
Padding can raise traffic and arithmetic work; a single launch can still win if it amortizes launch cost.
Configured and theoretical alignment helpers may differ on a pinned hardware/library snapshot.

headings: Worked routing example

concepts.title: JAX function transformations
concepts.meaning: JAX wraps a pure function with gradient, batching and compilation transformations over pytree state.
concepts.brief: Start with a pure scalar loss over structured parameter leaves. Derive gradients, batch the function with vmap, and compile a shape-specific call with jit, making each transformation visible as a callable wrapper.
pitfalls: Transformations derive callable functions; they are not sequential runtime lifecycle stages.
JIT specialization depends on compatible shapes and static control flow.

headings: Transform one small function at a time
Transformation order changes the derived program
Pytrees carry structured state
JIT compiles a shape-specific contract

concepts.title: Option-scoring decision readout
concepts.meaning: A decision readout scores the options that were actually offered and can preserve an abstain route.
concepts.brief: Encode state, question and offered options, then compare each option marker with a decision marker and normalize scores over that option set. Keep a contract-approved abstain branch and separate the public interface from undisclosed implementation details.
pitfalls: Kev’s public implementation does not establish Jev’s undisclosed architecture or training recipe.
Scores over offered options are not probabilities over every possible action.

headings: Three inspectable routes, one undisclosed model

concepts.title: Kernel candidate promotion gates
concepts.meaning: A candidate earns a performance claim only after correctness, safety, comparable timing and traffic checks.
concepts.brief: Move a candidate through the reference oracle, compilation, numerical and shape checks, sanitizer coverage, comparable timing and traffic sanity. Stop at the first failed gate and keep its evidence receipt.
pitfalls: Passing finite tests and sanitizer paths does not prove correctness over every input.
Performance claims require comparable timing scope and declared cache state.

headings: Six gates before a performance claim

concepts.title: Fused kernel traffic
concepts.meaning: Fusion keeps intermediate values local so adjacent operations avoid writing and rereading temporary tensors.
concepts.brief: Compare separate kernels that materialize and reread intermediate vectors with one fused kernel that holds intermediates in registers or a local tile. Show fewer global-memory trips beside the longer live range and occupancy cost.
pitfalls: Fusion can increase live ranges and register or local-memory pressure.
Fewer launches do not guarantee lower latency when spills add memory traffic.

concepts.title: Inspector-executor plan contract
concepts.meaning: A metadata plan assigns irregular requests to GPU tiles and workspace that a stable attention run consumes.
concepts.brief: Show three requests with different query lengths and scattered KV pages. A CPU-side inspector reads offsets and page metadata once, assigns tiles, sizes scratch workspace and decides whether to split KV work. The executor consumes the plan plus query/cache tensors, emits partial states when needed, then merges them. Animate compatibility checks for lengths, masks, pointer layout and workspace lifetime; distinguish a reusable plan from stale decode metadata.
pitfalls: A plan is reusable only across compatible batch specifications; decode lengths can change between steps.
Stable buffer addresses do not make stale metadata contents correct.
The pinned prefill plan performs host-side work and copies, so verify graph-capture constraints for the selected wrapper.

headings: Plan then run: inspector-executor for GPU kernels

concepts.title: Server-side LLM API request
concepts.meaning: An authenticated server turns a user task into a bounded provider request and records the result.
concepts.brief: Route a browser task through backend authentication, tenant authorization, trusted database facts, redaction and a typed provider request. Return a traceable result and show a retry reusing its idempotency key.
pitfalls: Provider credentials stay on the server and outside client bundles.
A timeout leaves the remote outcome uncertain; use idempotency and reconcile before repeating side effects.

headings: Keep credentials on the server
A task contract for the model
Timeouts, rate limits, and resilience
Idempotency and side-effect isolation

concepts.title: LLM lifecycle stages
concepts.meaning: A model moves from pre-training through post-training, evaluation, compression and deployment.
concepts.brief: Move a base checkpoint through post-training, versioned evaluation, optional compression and deployment. Keep evaluation as a release decision and feed failed evidence back to the candidate under review.
pitfalls: Evaluation can test an unchanged checkpoint and still change the release decision.
Compression may alter representation or retrain weights; evaluate the compressed candidate again.

headings: Five lifecycle stages, one key decision

concepts.title: ML release tuple
concepts.meaning: A release binds data, features, model, policy, monitor and rollback artifact before promotion.
concepts.brief: Bind snapshot, preprocessing, model, action policy and monitor into one release record. Advance a candidate through registration and canary evidence; promote only after gates pass and retain the previous tuple for rollback.
pitfalls: A model file alone cannot reproduce a decision when preprocessing and policy also changed.
Registering a candidate is distinct from promoting it to production.

headings: Define the shared release tuple

concepts.title: Unified-memory allocation
concepts.meaning: CPU and GPU share physical system memory while a device change can still create a distinct buffer.
concepts.brief: Compare discrete host RAM and device VRAM with Apple CPU and GPU sharing one physical pool. Show a separate MPS buffer allocation inside that pool, then add weights, cache and activations to the memory ledger.
pitfalls: Shared physical memory does not mean every tensor has identical device placement or allocation lifetime.
A Mac can run out of memory after model weights fit because runtime state and other apps also consume the pool.

headings: One memory pool, two PyTorch devices

concepts.title: Bounded production agent loop
concepts.meaning: Trusted admission, verified evidence and a bounded action precede a separately authorized write.
concepts.brief: Admit a trusted request, retrieve and verify evidence, check account state, draft a response and log the proposed action. Put a separate authorization checkpoint before a state-changing write.
pitfalls: A deep copy protects trusted runtime evidence from planner mutation but is not a process sandbox.
Context and model output do not grant authority.

headings: Execute approved writes separately

concepts.title: Python row to batch
concepts.meaning: A keyed record becomes a batch of rows whose labels feed an explicit comparison.
concepts.brief: Begin with one JSON record, map its keys to named Python values, normalize expected and predicted strings, and produce one Boolean. Expand the same transformation to a list only after the row contract is clear.
pitfalls: A dictionary lookup gives a field value; it does not validate the input schema by itself.
Keep a numeric score separate from its formatted display.

headings: One row is ordinary Python data
A list turns one row into a batch
Trace request 102 through the boundaries

concepts.title: Paired-seed experiment
concepts.meaning: Each random seed runs both arms, so the comparison uses matched within-seed differences.
concepts.brief: Run baseline and candidate under the same indexed seed, connect each pair, calculate per-seed differences and summarize uncertainty across those differences. Separate pilot seeds from confirmatory seeds.
pitfalls: Shared random draws do not guarantee positive covariance or lower variance.
Independent resampling of the two arms discards the pairing.

headings: The paired seed trial protocol

concepts.title: Runtime buffer lifetime
concepts.meaning: A copy-stream event orders a consumer stream, and the buffer remains alive through consumption and completion.
concepts.brief: Queue a copy on a producer stream, record a ready event and enqueue a consumer wait on another stream. Keep the allocation live through the consumer and release it only after dependent work completes.
pitfalls: A stream wait orders device work without blocking the host.
A wait on an unrecorded event represents empty prior work; record before waiting.

headings: Cross-stream coordination via events

concepts.title: Relational row join
concepts.meaning: Foreign keys connect rows across tables so a join can recover each chunk’s source.
concepts.brief: Connect a chunk row to its document through a foreign-key value and a join. Animate constraints rejecting a dangling source ID, then reopen the file-backed database to show committed relationships persist.
pitfalls: A join recovers relationships expressed by keys; it does not infer semantic relevance.
SQLite foreign-key enforcement must be enabled on the connection.

headings: Join a chunk to its source

concepts.title: From text to a useful prediction
concepts.meaning: An application collects input, calls a learned model, presents the prediction, and saves useful results.
concepts.brief: Follow one support message from a browser through an HTTP endpoint into a text classifier. Show the returned probability vector, the threshold that selects automatic handling or review, and the saved result. Keep model prediction separate from the routing decision.
pitfalls: A high model score needs measured calibration before it can be read as an observed success rate.
Application tests and labeled model evaluation answer different questions.

headings: Turn that prediction into an API
